traits.notes: The seedling exhibits opposite, simple, lanceolate leaves with entire margins. The stem is woody, smooth, and green to light brown. Tendrils are present at the tips of some branches, suggesting climbing or twining growth habit. Some leaves show minor damage (small holes or missing margins), but cause is not inferred. No stipules, latex, or pulvinus observed. Multiple images confirm consistent morphology across views.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clear paired leaves visible at each node along the stem in close-up views)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced along the stem with visible internodes, not clustered at the apex)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without subdivisions into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no teeth or serrations visible)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (narrow, elongated with a pointed apex and broader base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (sharply pointed tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapering to the petiole, wedge-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs lengthwise with lateral veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins clearly visible and run parallel to each other, close together)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface appears glossy, reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or pubescence on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, not elongated)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and slightly woody, not soft or herbaceous)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: green to light brown (stem is green in younger sections, transitioning to light brown in older parts)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf base)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base; not applicable as leaf is simple and not in Fabaceae)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): present (thin, coiled structures at tips of some stems, resembling tendrils)

F. Notes: The seedling exhibits opposite, simple, lanceolate leaves with entire margins. The stem is woody, smooth, and green to light brown. Tendrils are present at the tips of some branches, suggesting climbing or twining growth habit. Some leaves show minor damage (small holes or missing margins), but cause is not inferred. No stipules, latex, or pulvinus observed. Multiple images confirm consistent morphology across views.
